userPrompt:
On Windows, no program the application runs opens a window of its own. Every child process it starts on the host, git, piton (builds, slicing, its language server, fluency), podman, the harness and its one-off runs, a run target's shell, and the commands that stop a process, is started without a console window, so nothing flashes on screen while the application works, in a release build as in a development one. What these programs print is still read as ever. The login view's command, run under a pseudo-terminal, still works as the ContainerEnvironmentScope says.

Say this once, in the ApplicationScope, and give the reason: a release build on Windows is a GUI application with no console, so Windows gives every console program it starts a window of its own unless told not to.

In the code, start every child process through one shared helper that sets CREATE_NO_WINDOW on Windows (std::os::windows::process::CommandExt::creation_flags, 0x08000000) and does nothing elsewhere, and replace every direct std::process::Command::new in src with it, including container::podman_command and harness::one_off_command. Tests may keep using Command directly.

content.text:
Every program the app starts now goes through one shared helper that opens no console window on Windows, but I couldn't compile or test the Windows branch here. This machine has no Windows standard library, so check it with `cargo check --target x86_64-pc-windows-msvc` or a Windows build. On Linux the build is clean and all 479 tests pass; nothing changes on macOS or Linux.

- **The helper:** the new `src/process.rs` has `process::command(program)`. On Windows it sets `CREATE_NO_WINDOW` (`0x0800_0000`) through `CommandExt::creation_flags`; elsewhere it's a plain `Command::new`.
- **Replaced everywhere:** all 33 direct `Command::new` calls outside tests now use it. That covers git, piton (builds, slicing, the language server, fluency), podman (including `container::podman_command`), the harness and its one-off runs (`harness::one_off_command`, quick asks), run targets' `sh`/`cmd` shells, and the `kill`/`taskkill` used to stop processes. Output is still piped and read exactly as before.
- **Login view:** it already starts its command through `podman_command()`, so it's covered. Its pseudo-terminal is opened only on Unix and is unchanged; on Windows it uses pipes.
- **One exception:** the command palette uses a gpui UI component that is also called `Command`. My search-and-replace caught it, so I put it back; it isn't a process.
- **Tests:** they still create `Command` directly, as the prompt allows.

The constraints are in `.suspense/history/1791089897-HideConsoleWindowsForChildProcesses2.understanding.md`.
